comps: Marks
Pieces 3 x 30 = 90; Technical requirements 21; Sight-reading 21; Aural tests 18; total 150. Pass 100, Merit 120, Distinction 130 (Below Pass 50-99). Pass in each component not required.
Choosing pieces

Percussion (Combined), Grades 1-8: one piece each from List A (Snare Drum), B (Timpani) and C (Tuned Percussion); up to two pieces by same composer; at Grades 1-3 at least one piece must be accompanied (live piano or percussion, no recordings). Technical requirements: candidate chooses ONE of Snare Drum studies, Timpani studies or Tuned Percussion scales and arpeggios, and tells the examiner; sight-reading subject is chosen by the examiner, so instruments for all three must be available. Acoustic instruments only. Timpani drums needed (Combined): piece/study G1-4 two, G5 three, G6 three, G7-8 four; sight-reading two drums G1-5, three G6-7, four G8. Tuned percussion: xylophone, marimba, vibraphone, glockenspiel (G1-2 only); G6-8 pieces must use the specified instrument. Syllabus valid from 1 Jan 2020; same lists as Performance Grades but not same pieces for both. No Initial Grade for percussion.
Digital exams

Practical Grades are face-to-face visit exams; Performance Grades (separate, offered as remote video assessment) share the repertoire lists but pieces cannot be repeated for the same grade and marks cannot transfer.
sections: Scales & technical work

Candidate chooses ONE option and tells the examiner. (1) SNARE DRUM: Snare drum study: two studies (A and B) prepared, examiner picks one; each based on a set of rudiments listed on the sheet music (rudiments not itemised in the syllabus text); any sticking; not from memory. (2) TIMPANI: Timpani study: two studies (Study A and B) prepared, examiner picks one; 2 drums; all rests of crotchet length or longer damped; may be played on A and D (any perfect 4th) as teacher may tune. (3) TUNED PERCUSSION (scales played from memory on one instrument; hand to hand except thirds/sixths/octaves; no vibraphone pedal; free starting octave): C, F, G majors; A, D, E minors (natural, harmonic or melodic, at choice): scales and arpeggios, 1 oct, hand to hand, even notes.
Sight-reading

Half a minute to look through. Examiner chooses Snare Drum, Timpani or Tuned Percussion. Snare: 4 bars (6 in 2/4), 4/4 3/4 2/4; h q iq iiiq, semiquaver groupings, rests, f/p. Timpani: 4 bars (6 in 2/4); 2 drums tuned A and d; perfect-4th intervals; basic note values; f/p. Tuned: 4 bars (6 in 2/4); C, F major; range d'-g''; single treble stave, max two mallets; f/mf.
Aural & other tests
Grade 1 aural: (A) clap pulse, say 2 or 3 time; (B) sing 3 two-bar echoes (major, tonic-mediant); (C) spot a pitch change (near beginning/end); (D) questions on dynamics and articulation.

exams.full: Associate of the Royal Schools of Music — ABRSM Level 4 Diploma in Music Performance
exams.syllabus: RQF Level 4 (EQF 5), about the end of the first year of an undergraduate course; 90 credits, 54 GLH, 900 TQT
comps: Entry requirement

A pass at Grade 8 on the same or a closely related instrument: ABRSM Practical or Performance Grade 8, or an accepted equivalent from another board (for example Trinity, LCM, MTB, Guildhall, RIAM, AMEB or UNISA). No theory prerequisite.
Format & marks

Face-to-face (public venue or private visit) OR digital (video recorded at a time and place of the candidate's choice, with no fixed sessions; video uploaded at booking or within 28 days). Performance only: 30-minute programme (±2 min), timed from the first note to the last. Marks: pieces 30 (60%) + performance as a whole 20 (40%) = 50. Distinction 45–50, Merit 40–44, Pass 34–39, Below Pass 17–33.
Programme rules

At least 20 minutes from the ARSM repertoire list for the instrument, plus up to 10 minutes of own-choice music at Grade 8 standard or above. No written or spoken elements and no other tests (no viva, no programme notes, no quick study). Candidates submit a programme form, or enter programme details online for digital exams.
sections: About the repertoire list

Official ARSM repertoire list for percussion (combined), read from the ABRSM PDF (12 entries in 4 sections). Candidates must present a programme which includes at least one work from three of the four sections (Tuned Percussion, Timpani, Snare Drum, Multiple Percussion). Own-choice music is also allowed within the programme rules above. Check the board's current list before entering; lists are updated online.
General notes

Pathway as of Oct 2026: ARSM (L4) → LRSM (L6) → FRSM (L7). DipABRSM is withdrawn (last date 31 Dec 2023). The old-format LRSM closed 30 Apr 2024 and the old FRSM closed 31 Oct 2024. All three current diplomas require only Grade 8 in the instrument (ABRSM or an equivalent board for LRSM/FRSM). No Grade 5 or 6 theory prerequisite is stated for any current performance diploma. Under the old syllabus, Grade 5 theory appeared only as a condition on some substitutions. ARSM has no written element. LRSM/FRSM need a written (2,000 / 3,500 words) or spoken-video (10 / 17 min) supporting-evidence submission. Digital exams have no fixed sessions: book, pay and upload any time; for digital ARSM the video goes in at booking or within 28 days. Specific LRSM/FRSM upload windows weren't stated in the spec, which refers to abrsm.org/how-to-book. ABRSM discontinued printed diploma syllabuses, and lists are updated online, so re-check the abrsm.org pages before entering. abrsm.org HTML pages returned redirect errors to the fetch tool, so some details come from the PDFs and ABRSM's Taiwan mirror.
General rules (all instruments)

Both LRSM and FRSM programmes must be balanced and varied: a variety of moods, keys and tempi and at least two pieces or movements contrasting by period or style. Works and movements must be played complete unless the repertoire list says otherwise, and any list-specific instructions must be followed. Music published with an accompaniment must be performed with one; any suitable instrument may accompany provided the candidate stays the main soloist, candidates arrange their own accompanist, and pre-recorded accompaniments are not allowed unless the composer intended them. Memory is not required (but encouraged if it helps). Any edition matching the list entry may be used and own-choice music must exist as a legible, fully notated score; performing from unauthorised photocopies of copyright editions is not allowed. Own-choice may include the candidate's own composition or arrangement but must still be at or above the required standard, and ABRSM cannot give prior approval of own-choice standard. An audience is encouraged but not required. Infringements (wrong length, too much own choice without approval, wrong movements, edited video) can bring a warning, mark deduction or disqualification. A video can only ever be submitted once, and the same Unit 2 work cannot be reused at a higher level.

Candidates should perform at least one work from three of the four sections (Tuned Percussion, Timpani, Snare Drum, Multiple Percussion/Other), including at least one item on a tuned percussion instrument. Own-choice music is also allowed within the programme rules above. Check the board's current list before entering; lists are updated online.
General notes

Pathway as of Oct 2026: ARSM (L4) → LRSM (L6) → FRSM (L7). DipABRSM is withdrawn (last date 31 Dec 2023). The old-format LRSM closed 30 Apr 2024 and the old FRSM closed 31 Oct 2024. All three current diplomas require only Grade 8 in the instrument (ABRSM or an equivalent board for LRSM/FRSM). No Grade 5 or 6 theory prerequisite is stated for any current performance diploma. Under the old syllabus, Grade 5 theory appeared only as a condition on some substitutions. ARSM has no written element. LRSM/FRSM need a written (2,000 / 3,500 words) or spoken-video (10 / 17 min) supporting-evidence submission. Digital exams have no fixed sessions: book, pay and upload any time; for digital ARSM the video goes in at booking or within 28 days. Specific LRSM/FRSM upload windows weren't stated in the spec, which refers to abrsm.org/how-to-book. ABRSM discontinued printed diploma syllabuses, and lists are updated online, so re-check the abrsm.org pages before entering. abrsm.org HTML pages returned redirect errors to the fetch tool, so some details come from the PDFs and ABRSM's Taiwan mirror.
General rules (all instruments)

Both LRSM and FRSM programmes must be balanced and varied: a variety of moods, keys and tempi and at least two pieces or movements contrasting by period or style. Works and movements must be played complete unless the repertoire list says otherwise, and any list-specific instructions must be followed. Music published with an accompaniment must be performed with one; any suitable instrument may accompany provided the candidate stays the main soloist, candidates arrange their own accompanist, and pre-recorded accompaniments are not allowed unless the composer intended them. Memory is not required (but encouraged if it helps). Any edition matching the list entry may be used and own-choice music must exist as a legible, fully notated score; performing from unauthorised photocopies of copyright editions is not allowed. Own-choice may include the candidate's own composition or arrangement but must still be at or above the required standard, and ABRSM cannot give prior approval of own-choice standard. An audience is encouraged but not required. Infringements (wrong length, too much own choice without approval, wrong movements, edited video) can bring a warning, mark deduction or disqualification. A video can only ever be submitted once, and the same Unit 2 work cannot be reused at a higher level.
Other components

Unit 2 is a written submission (2000 words, plus or minus 10%, as PDF) or a spoken video presentation (10 minutes, plus or minus 10%) on one of four options: Informing your audience, Detailed programme analysis (a 20-minute section of the programme), Programming your performance, or Preparation for performance. It must include reflection and evaluation. The first page of each own-choice piece is uploaded as PDF. Written work needs a front page with Contact ID, instrument, option, date and word count; a candidate declaration of genuine work is required.

exams.name: ATCL
exams.full: Associate of Trinity College London (Music Performance)
comps: Entry requirement
None formal: no minimum age, no prior grade or theory qualification required.
Format & marks

Available face-to-face (at Trinity centres, no audience) and digital (one continuous unedited video, max 3GB, uploaded with written programme, any approval letter and one scan per piece; audience allowed). Same structure, criteria and certificate in both formats. Recital 32-38 min performing time (exam slot 40 min). Marked out of 100: Recital 96 (Fluency & accuracy 32, Technical assurance & application 32, Musical sense & communication 32) + Programme & planning 4 (written programme 2, planning/balance/construction 2). Results: Distinction 80-100, Pass 60-79, Below Pass 1 45-59, Below Pass 2 0-44. No Merit band.
Programme rules

Programme of at least two works (singing/percussion three), showing a range of moods, styles and tempi; any order. Works complete unless the list specifies movements. Programme may be all list repertoire, list + own-choice, or all own-choice; any own-choice (or single movements of works listed as complete) must be pre-approved as a whole programme via trinitycollege.com/approvals. Accompanied candidates may include unaccompanied works up to 40% of the programme. No viva/discussion component is mentioned in the March 2026 syllabus. Written programme (composers, titles, timings) required; no full programme notes at ATCL. Trinity describes ATCL as equivalent to a first-year undergraduate recital.

General notes

No Grade 8 or Theory of Music prerequisite for any performance diploma (Trinity entry-requirements page and March 2026 syllabus). Current documents: 'Classical Music Performance Diplomas' syllabus, online edition March 2026 (resource id 8556, same for all instruments; Trinity points to trinitycollege.com/performance-diplomas for the current version) and 2026-edition instrument repertoire lists. Digital diplomas (ATCL, LTCL) allow recorded/backing-track accompaniment; face-to-face exams need a live accompanist. Own-choice programme approval: whole programme only, usually within 15 working days; the syllabus says the approval letter is valid 3 years, while a support article says 2 years (conflict, check the letter). Works on any current Trinity grade, certificate or lower-diploma list cannot be own-choice, and a work approved for one diploma cannot be reused at a higher diploma. Up to 30 s allowance for unshortened introductions/tuttis; gaps between movements about 10 s. Short programmes may be penalised.com resource IDs were mis-identified by the fetch tool, but every list used here was confirmed by its heading and by at least two consistent fetches.
General rules (all instruments)

Applies to all instruments. Performance times cover all works including short breaks between movements (about 10 seconds maximum) but not between works; the minimum has no leeway and under-length recitals are referred and penalised, while over-length ones may be curtailed. Programmes show a range of moods, styles and tempi. Use only one instrument type (family members such as flute and piccolo allowed; for flute at most one piece on piccolo or alto flute). Unaccompanied works may make up to 40% of an accompanied programme (one long listed work above 40% is accepted); pieces published with accompaniment may not be played unaccompanied; the candidate provides one accompanist (normally). Repeats: observe da capo and dal segno but do not play exposition or recapitulation repeats, repeats of more than two bars, or repeats within variations (Baroque suite repeats are allowed only if musically justified by ornamentation). Long introductions, endings and tuttis must be shortened (up to 30 seconds allowed). All cadenzas should be played. Memory is not required and earns no marks; metronomes and spoken introductions are not allowed. Music must be from a reliable, unaltered edition and legal copies are needed (copies for the examiner, and originals shown). Stagecraft is marked. A written programme (names, date, composers, full titles with movements and opus numbers, timing per piece and total, in order) is required.
Other components

Programme and planning section: a written programme (2 marks) and planning, balance and construction of the programme (2 marks). No viva, quick study or written submission; detailed notes are not required at ATCL.
